summary: This is a port of a kernel that was hand-landed on moe master after measuring 10.6/11.4 us of align become 4.0/6.9 us. In decode it stands on its own: the T>32 overlap is gone (moe-chain-cuda-swapab-expert-once-large-t failed tests), and the result can be read from the align and Marlin kernel rows at verify_16/32 without a companion, though the headline will be inside the CI.
justification: Mechanism: at T=128/256 (verify_16/32, the only shapes on the T>32 path) master runs the expert_map gather (index_elementwise) and SGLang moe_align_block_size (align kernel plus count_and_sort, and in decode with num_experts=N_EXPERTS=256, not 32). That is 3-4 launches. One 33-program Triton launch replaces them. The moe parent measured this directly: 10.6->4.0 us at bs=128 and 11.4->6.9 us at bs=256, +4.3%/+3.2% per shape, deterministic integer work. So the kernel-level claim is about as safe as a port gets. Size: Marlin is 51-70% of verify_16/32 (272-450 us), while the shapes run 447-911 us against floors of 127-267 us. Saving 4-8 us is +0.6-1.5% per verify shape and roughly +0.3-0.4% on the 6-load geomean, well inside the >=1.5% CI. The hypothesis says this itself, and the run must be judged on the kernel rows. The expected directions agree with TASK.md: verify_16/32 faster, decode_* and verify_1 (T<=32, kernel R path, DL_MAX_TOKENS=32) byte-identical and usable as an in-run drift control. Weakest link 1: the decode numbers are borrowed. FINDINGS lists only the top 3 kernels per shape, so decode's own align+gather time at T>32 is not in evidence. Decode's SGLang align runs the 256-expert variant (a 256-bin cumsum, capacity n+256*(bsm-1)), which may be slower than moe's 32-expert one (so the gain could be larger) and may size Marlin's block list differently. Read the removed rows from this run's profile, not from moe. Weakest link 2: the change keeps `(topk_ids - local_start) % N_EXPERTS` in kernel_fn (a subtract and a remainder launch) and passes local_start=0. Only the gather and the align go away, so expect 2-3 launches removed, not 4. Two smaller points: (a) bsm above 32 tokens is always 16 under the cap (T*8/32/16 < 0.9 never holds for T>=33 with bsm 8), so only the BSM=16 variant is reachable. The moe parent timed bsm 16 at bs=128 but 32 at bs=256, so the T=256 kernel time at BSM 16 (more padding and block_experts stores) is not measured, though it should be within ~1 us. (b) Capacity changes from 256-expert (n+3840 slots, 304 blocks at T=128) to 32-expert (n+480, ~94 blocks). If Marlin's grid or early-exit depends on block_experts.numel() rather than n_padded, the Marlin rows can move too. That still belongs to this change, but the harvester must compare Marlin rows base vs hyp, not only the align rows.
confounders: marlin-block-m-cap-16: fixes bsm=16 at T=128 and T=256 (the moe parent used 16/32). This sets the kernel's padding and block counts and the BSM variant compiled. It does not confound attribution, but the T=256/BSM16 kernel time is unmeasured, and a later retune of the cap must recompile and re-check this kernel.

sglang-pipeline-parity-router-hilo-m8: sets decode's T>32 contract (expert_map gather plus moe_align_block_size(..., N_EXPERTS=256)) that is being replaced. The new 32-expert capacity and n_padded can change what Marlin iterates over. This is a legitimate part of the change, but it is a second possible source of Marlin-row movement besides the removed launches.

post-expert-norm-triton-small-t: gated below 32 tokens, so no timing confound at T>32. Correctness dependency only: fused_post_expert_norm_weighted_sum(slot_expert_ids=local_ids) and silu_and_mul(expert_ids=local_ids) need int32 contiguous local_ids with exactly -1 for remote routes, which program 32 writes.
small-t-launch-minimal-dense-chain-pdl: T<=32 only (DL_MAX_TOKENS=32). It does not interact with the T>32 path. Its shapes are this run's untouched drift control.
interference: No companion is warranted. The change replaces 3-4 small integer launches on the T>32 main-stream path with one launch. No landed hypothesis sits between that and its measurement: the cap-16 pick only sets BSM, and an ab-revert or ab-tune of it would shift the new kernel by under 1 us and could not flip the reading. The headline gain (~0.3-0.4%) is below resolution, and no A/B companion fixes that. The interpretable signal is in this single run's top_kernels at verify_16/32: the new _align_parallel_kernel row against the removed index_elementwise / moe_align_block_size_kernel / count_and_sort rows from the base profile (81ee6714b7614a99), plus a check that the Marlin rows did not move in the wrong direction. T<=32 shapes are byte-identical and serve as the drift control. A control that splits the gather removal from the align replacement is pointless, because one kernel does both. Harvest rule: hand-land if the log shows '[align-parallel-large-t] ON' with 0 real mismatches, the new row is at or below the sum of the removed rows minus ~2 us at both verify shapes, and the verify_16/32 paired ratios are at or above base, even if classify says neutral (as the moe parent did).
rules_flags: None blocking. The host branch is on num_tokens (shape) only. local_start=0 and local_count=32 are constants, not values derived from inputs. The data-dependent (topk_ids - local_start) % 256 stays a device op in kernel_fn. Outputs are allocated fresh per call, no syncs inside kernel_fn, and the self-check syncs are in prepare() only.

Gate align_par_ok on structural mismatches only (per-expert route sets, block counts, n_padded vs local_ids, the -1 tail, the sentinel). Never gate on capacity or n_padded-vs-SGLang: decode's SGLang reference is the 256-expert align, so capacity always differs (LESSONS: a capacity-counting gate silently measures master). Reusing the existing _dl_align_problems(local_ids, align, bsm, tag), which already compares only what Marlin consumes, is the safest comparator.
Every tl.arange size must stay a power of 2 (copy is verbatim: CHUNK 512, NUM_E 32, PAD_BLOCK next_pow2(BSM), BLK 64). Fine at BSM 16.
open_questions: How long do decode's own gather + 256-expert moe_align_block_size + count_and_sort take at T=128/256? Take this from the base profile's full kernel list, not from FINDINGS' top 3. It is the denominator for judging the new row.

Is Marlin's work bounded by n_padded on device or by block_experts.numel() / sorted_ids.numel()? If the latter, shrinking capacity from 256-expert to 32-expert sizing could save Marlin time too, and the Marlin rows should be read as part of this change.

Follow-up, not this run: load local_start from data['local_start'] (an int32 [1] device tensor) inside the kernel and consume raw global topk_ids. That would also drop the subtract and remainder launches (~2 more graph nodes), as kernel R already does at T<=32.

Should the self-check also run the Marlin y comparison (y_new vs y_ref via _experts with both aligns), as _dl_self_check does for kernel R? That would catch a layout error that the structural check misses, at a few seconds of prepare time.
The test case 'batch 33, ctx 20000, layer full' (T=33, bsm 16) and the q_len-8 tests at T=24..40 exercise the new path at small n. Confirm the 'ON' line in the log before trusting the timings.
